artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q$ be a smooth manifold of dimension $n$ with local coordinates $x = (x^1,\dots,x^n)$, and let $T^*Q$ denote its cotangent bundle with induced canonical coordinates $(x,p) = (x^1,\dots,x^n,p_1,\dots,p_n)$. Let $\theta = p_i\,dx^i$ be the Liouville one-form and $\omega_0 = -d\theta = dx^i\wedge dp_i$ the canonical symplectic form on $T^*Q$.

A locally conformal symplectic (LCS) structure on $T^*Q$ is a pair $(\Omega,\eta)$ consisting of a non-degenerate two-form $\Omega$ and a closed one-form $\eta$ (the Lee form) satisfying $d\Omega = \eta\wedge\Omega$. Write $\eta = \bar\eta_{x^i}\,dx^i + \bar\eta_{p_i}\,dp_i + f\,dt$-type pieces; concretely, decompose the spatial Lee form on $T^*Q$ as $\bar\eta = \bar\eta_{x^i}\,dx^i + \bar\eta_{p_i}\,dp_i$, and let $f$ be the time-component (conformal factor) coefficient appearing in the time-dependent LCS framework.

Given a smooth Hamiltonian $H : \mathbb{R}\times T^*Q \to \mathbb{R}$, the associated locally conformal symplectic equations of motion for a curve $t\mapsto (x(t),p(t))$ are
$$\dot x^i \;=\; \frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i} \;+\; \bigl(p_j\,\dot x^j - H\bigr)\,\bar\eta_{p_i},$$
$$\dot p_i \;=\; -\frac{\partial H}{\partial x^i} \;+\; f\,p_i \;-\; \bigl(p_j\,\dot x^j - H\bigr)\,\bar\eta_{x^i}.$$

Question: Exhibit a concrete physical or mechanical system whose dynamics is governed by the above system, and provide a physical/mechanical interpretation of the additional terms $(p_j\dot x^j - H)\bar\eta_{p_i}$, $f p_i$, and $-(p_j\dot x^j - H)\bar\eta_{x^i}$ that distinguish these equations from standard Hamilton's equations.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature on locally conformal symplectic (LCS) Hamiltonian dynamics develops the geometric formalism on cotangent bundles and discusses dissipative-type extensions of Hamilton's equations, with potential applications via contact pairs and Lie systems (engineering, control, cosmology). However, no source unambiguously identifies a canonical physical example fitting precisely the time-dependent LCS equations stated, nor a definitive physical interpretation; the question is interpretive/open-ended and its status is unclear.

status_evidence.title: Time-dependent Hamiltonian mechanics on a locally conformal symplectic manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Develops Hamilton-Jacobi and time-dependent Hamiltonian formalism on LCS manifolds, but treats the geometric framework rather than specifying a canonical physical example.
status_evidence.claim: LCS time-dependent Hamiltonian dynamics is studied geometrically; concrete physical examples are not pinpointed.

status_evidence.title: Discrete Dynamics on Locally Conformal Framework
status_evidence.snippet: LCS Hamilton's equations on cotangent bundles are formulated and discretized via Legendre transform; potential applications via contact pairs and Lie systems are mentioned.
status_evidence.claim: Applications to engineering/control via Lie systems are suggested but no definitive mechanical model for the stated equations is given.

status_evidence.title: Conformal symplectic geometry of cotangent bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Studies conformal symplectic structure on cotangent bundles from a geometric viewpoint.
status_evidence.claim: Mathematical framework is established; physical interpretation of LCS equations of motion is not the focus.
